title: Downscaled and debiased climate simulations for North America from 21,000 years ago to 2100AD
problem: The use of varying downscaling methods and observational baselines among researchers produces confounding biases in climate simulations, hindering the seamless integration of past and future climate data required for ecological modeling.
method: This paper presents a method for creating unified, debiased, and downscaled climate simulations for North America from 21,000 years ago to 2100 AD by applying a common downscaling and debiasing approach to paleoclimatic and future simulations against a single observational baseline.
task: The task is to create unified datasets of debiased and downscaled climate simulations for North America, spanning from 21,000 years ago to 2100 AD, suitable for modeling the effects of past and future climate change on species distributions and diversity.
innovation: This paper presents unified datasets of debiased and downscaled climate simulations for North America from 21,000 years ago to 2100 AD, providing a common set of simulations suitable for seamlessly modeling the effects of past and future climate change on species distributions and diversity.
